A1.justification: Both PDFs describe H2OFlow and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Shared content can be matched reliably despite figure renumbering, appendix reorganization, and substantial additions in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original OMOMO and BEHAVE evaluations, ablations, runtime measurements, and qualitative real-object results, including Tables 1 and 3–5.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds downstream inference results, quantitative real-object comparisons, denoising experiments, and augmentation and language-conditioning examples.

M1.justification: The original object-conditioned flow model is retained, but Appendix P.2 adds a substantive language-conditioned variant: a frozen CLIP text encoder, text cross-attention in DiT blocks, training-time text dropout, and guided sampling. Figure 12 demonstrates prompt-dependent affordances. This changes the model's inputs and inference capabilities, rather than merely documenting the existing method.

E1.justification: V2 adds HOI region retrieval and pose selection as evaluated downstream tasks. Appendix P broadens training beyond CHOIS manipulation episodes to usage interactions such as sitting and leaning, and evaluates prompt-conditioned sitting versus moving a chair. OMOMO, BEHAVE, and real-object coverage already existed in v1; the new real-object scores alone are not a new domain.

E2.justification: The external comparison methods, including COMA, COMA-Recon, IAGNet, and DECO, are retained. New Table 2 introduces internal comparison variants using contact alone, contact plus orientation, contact plus spatial affordance, and shuffled affordances against the complete representation. The newly cited HOI generators are training-data sources, not evaluated competing baselines.

E3.justification: V2 adds downstream scoring and evaluation using normalized affordance fusion, retrieval mAP, pose-selection accuracy, collisions, and contact leakage. Appendix O introduces a six-object protocol with ICP alignment, synthetic CHOIS reference poses, MMD, coverage at 15 cm, and Frechet Pose Distance, plus controlled denoising sweeps with fixed model weights. The original splits and main training settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Table 2 tests the contribution of orientation and spatial information, including shuffled controls. Appendix O.2 tests sensitivity to denoising strength, while Figures 9 and 12 examine usage-data augmentation and prompt conditioning on a chair. These substantially extend the retained cross-attention, occlusion, and flow-versus-SMPL analyses.

E5.justification: The existing uncertainty entries are retained, and new Table 2 uses the same unexplained ± reporting style. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, or whether these spreads are standard deviations or standard errors. V2 adds no confidence intervals, significance tests, or documented uncertainty-estimation procedure; Table 7 reports point estimates.

E6.justification: The original benchmark, occlusion, and runtime values remain unchanged. V2 adds substantial results: Table 2 reports Top-5 pose-selection accuracy of 0.64 for all affordances versus 0.41 for contact alone, and Table 7 reports synthetic-reference coverage of 64.5% for H2OFlow versus 43.2% for COMA. New denoising results and augmentation/prompt visualizations provide further findings. These are newly reported comparisons, not v1-to-v2 same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 introduces a mathematical fusion score for downstream inference and a text-conditioned noise-combination rule in Appendix P.2. The original flow and affordance definitions and SMPL/cross-embodiment optimization, including Equations 1–16, remain unchanged. No new theorem or proof is supplied; the standard pose-distance formulas principally document the added evaluation.

C1.justification: The scientific abstract, three introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: learning contact, orientation, and spatial affordances from synthetic data through point-cloud flows, with generalization to unseen real objects. The added experiments and appendix extensions do not redefine those main contributions.

C2.justification: V2 interprets shuffled controls as evidence that structured orientation and spatial information matter beyond additional features. It newly identifies CHOIS's moving/lifting bias and explains how usage data changes learned affordances. Appendix O qualifies real-world scores as complementary synthetic-reference evidence and explains how aggressive denoising removes thin structures. These materially expand the interpretation and applicability boundaries, although the original limitations paragraph is retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds detailed Open3D outlier-removal procedures and parameter presets, real-object alignment instructions, augmentation preprocessing, and PyTorch listings for original and text-conditioned DiT blocks. Existing training hyperparameters are unchanged. It removes the abstract's explicit code/data release statement, although the project-site video link remains. Some new settings, including fusion weights and text-dropout/guidance values, remain unspecified.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting usage-data sources and text conditioning, including InteractAnything, HOI-PAGE, PICO, CLIP, and classifier-free guidance, plus scattered citations in existing passages. The central positioning against COMA remains intact, with a new statement that it is the only prior multi-affordance method. Some added attributions are poorly matched: Appendix J appends Kalman-filter references to the IAGNet and DECO discussion.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative remain unchanged. V2 integrates the former appendix overview into the main text, adds analysis and extension sections, updates cross-references, and makes localized clarifications such as replacing 'video sequences' with 'mesh sequences.' Conference headers and acknowledgements are added. The scientific additions do not constitute an extensive rewrite of retained material.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the visual evidence with downstream and real-object result tables, a denoising-preset display, augmentation and prompt comparisons, and two implementation figures. The old overview Figure 5 becomes main-text Figure 2, and old Figure 3 becomes Figure 4 with score color bars. Existing appendix displays are relocated and resized; Figure 11's caption is awkwardly separated from its code by Figure 12.

improvement.justification: V2 provides useful evidence missing from v1: Table 2 directly tests downstream benefits of non-contact affordances with component and shuffled controls, while Appendix O documents denoising sensitivity and acknowledges the limits of synthetic-reference real-world scores. These strengthen support and transparency. The net gain is limited by incompletely specified new settings, the apparently reversed conditional/unconditional weighting in the text-guidance equation, and poorly matched added citations. The additions therefore improve the paper, but do not establish a substantial overall quality gain.
